newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures steady at firm levels, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures steady at firm levels, rangebound.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were steady at slightly higher levels on Thursday and traders said the market was bound for the moment in a fairly narrow range.
June Brent crude was worth $18.17 a barrel at 1143 GMT, 11 cents up from the last close, while May gas oil was $1.50 higher at $164.50.
"There is nothing new on the fundamentals in the last little while," one IPE broker said.
"We saw it down to $17.81 yesterday and there is support there. We have seen selling up at around $18.25-$18.30 and I expect to see the same thing again today."
He said news from the Middle East was having relatively little impact on the market for now, although other traders felt it had buoyed prices a little.

Kuwait's official news agency said late on Wednesday that an Iraqi boat had opened fire on two Kuwaiti vessels some time this month. This follows news earlier in the week that Iraqi helicopters had flown pilgrims inside the allied no-fly zone.

GNI research said in a daily report: "On its own this (Kuwaiti boat issue) does not seem like a major incident, but combined with the no-fly issue, the U.N. may be forced to take action against this increased belligerence by the Iraqi regime."
The report added: "Some experts now talk of 'sanctions fatigue' among the international community, with several states keen to do business with the country. Iraqi oil is also popular with refiners."

Iraq's oil minister said told a news conference in Rome on Thursday talks with Italian companies were at "a very advanced stage" and that he expected to sign another deal with China soon. This follows news of deals with other countries pending the lifting of U.N. sanctions.
A broker said this news was not having any immediate impact on the market, however.
"This is all background although people are taking note of what is going on."
Traders also noted that U.S. products futures were likely to continue to exert a strong influence on world energy markets.
